author: DailyMail
title: Longshot Democratic candidate for Congress in Hawaii charged with felonies after beach fight
text:
Kirill Basin, 40, has been charged with two felonies for allegedly threatening a stranger with a knife during a fight on Keawakapu Beach in Maui on Saturday.
A longshot Democratic candidate for Congress in Hawaii has been seen hurling a chair at a stranger during an altercation about the volume of the music he was blaring on a public beach.
Kirill Basin, 40, was caught on camera fighting Kama Homan, 41, on Keawakapu Beach in Maui on Saturday after yelling and swearing at a group of bystanders. Basin has been charged with two felonies for allegedly threatening Homan with a knife, according to a criminal complaint seen by the Daily Mail. A lawyer for Basin indicated in court on Tuesday that he intends to plead not guilty to two charges of making terroristic threats.
Maui Police said the beach altercation unfolded after a 61-year-old man approached Basin and asked him to turn his music down. Basin responded by saying he had a firearm and would shoot the man's wife, according to police. Footage of the moments after this argument showed Kama intervening by squaring up to Basin, who shoved him. Kama said at that point, he deployed his mixed martial art skills.
Homan knocked Basin out at the end of the fight, as shown in the video footage. Basin is also accused of pulling out a knife and threatening several people with it, before tossing it into the ocean. Kama retrieved the six-inch switchblade from the shore and gave it to officers. Basin's lawyer disputed this, saying there's no evidence that he ever had a knife in his possession.
Basin also squared up to several beachgoers in the moments before the fight, video shows. Basin was also hit with terroristic threat charges in May after he allegedly walked into a government building and pulled a firearm on two employees. It is unclear why Basin allegedly entered the government building or who he threatened, however police said it followed a string of bizarre behavior from the congressional candidate.
Two days before his arrest, Basin was escorted from a South Maui town hall meeting after allegedly getting into a hostile argument with Councilmember Tom Cook and his staff. Cook's executive assistant Jared Agtunong alleged that after Basin was hauled out of the town hall, he then confronted Agtunong in the parking lot and police were forced to intervene. Basin has denied all the allegations and filed a lawsuit saying he was wrongfully arrested over the town hall altercation
